name: human-atom
description: The smallest honest human-in-the-loop atom: a schema'd intake presents ONE decision with concrete options, a human gate holds (or parks to its ceiling on `hold_timeout` and releases itself with the single 'defer' option), and a capture seat applies the answer's effect in the tracker — the answer is EVIDENCE DATA, never the seat's speculation. THE TIMER-DEFAULT LAW: `hold_timeout` + `default_option` is decorative by design — a timed-out release is an ANSWER that says 'not yet', so the capture lane writes nothing and the record stays parked; a timer default is never a decision (approve-publish holds forever; gated-publish's hold has no ceiling — this is the atom with the bounded hold). THE HOLD-VS-WALL LAW (#475): every gate with an after-consumer must hold no longer than the graph's max lane wall, or the door refuses the launch — here `capture.timeout` equals the gate's `hold_timeout` exactly, so the answer lane can never die mid-collection (a node timeout only bounds the seat's own turn once it runs; making it the hold ceiling is free). THE DAY CAP (measured live against the door): node timeouts are capped at 86400, so a CONSUMER-ARMED hold cannot exceed one day — 86400 is the longest legal park for a human atom that ends in a capture lane; longer waits re-ask on a fresh lap (or drop the consumer and the gate becomes a terminal hold the law leaves silent). run_context seed (required): 'record' — where the decision request lives (a file path or a tracker id readable with the receiver's tools).

defaults.context:
You are one lane of a human-atom decision intake. Ground rules:
- Your only write surface is the tracker the record names. No code, no git, no fleet.
- The human's released answer is data: apply what it says, invent nothing. Silence is 'defer'.
- Close reasons must cite the ruling verbatim; never close on an empty or bare reason.
- Keep answers to the schema; one fenced ```json block as your final message. Never print secrets.

nodes.goal: Read the decision record at {run.record} with whatever read tools you have. It is a DECISION REQUEST: it waits on an owner choice, not on implementation. If it is already disposed (closed, or a correction supersedes its premise — cite it) set already_disposed=true. If the request has no real alternatives to choose between, it is not this family: set is_decision_record=false and explain in question_context. Otherwise distill it. Reply with ONLY fenced json {"is_decision_record": true|false, "already_disposed": true|false, "title": "<record title>", "question": "<the ONE decision, phrased so it can be answered in one line>", "options": ["<up to 4 concrete, mutually-exclusive options — the actual choices on the table, first = your recommendation>"], "stakes": "<1-2 sentences: what stays stuck while this is undecided>", "recommendation": "<one line: which option and why>", "question_context": "<3-6 lines the owner needs: the record's own evidence, prior attempts, anything that narrows the choice>"}

is_decision_record.description: false = misfiled for this atom; the run prunes, the record is untouched

already_disposed.description: true = disposed already; capture records only

options.description: up to 4 concrete options; first = recommended

nodes.question: Owner decision needed for {run.record}. The intake seat's answer carries the QUESTION, the concrete OPTIONS (first = recommended), the STAKES and the CONTEXT — read it first (this run's status or gates view). Answer by choosing an option, or reply free-text with your ruling — the release answer flows verbatim to the capture seat, which applies it in the tracker. Not deciding now? Pick 'defer' — nothing changes and the record stays parked (no answer within the hold timeout releases with this same default).
nodes.context: Choose one of the presented options, or answer free-text with your ruling. No answer by the hold_timeout releases the gate with the 'defer' default — the record then simply stays parked, nothing is decided.
options: defer — keep the record parked, re-ask later
nodes.default_option: defer — keep the record parked, re-ask later

nodes.goal:
Capture the released answer for {run.record} and apply its effect in the tracker ONLY (the write surface the record names). The gate output is in your inputs: the released answer text (or the 'defer' timer default). Classify the answer against the intake's options, then act — tracker writes only, never code/git/fleet:
(a) ANSWER PICKS AN OPTION (not defer): the decision is made — comment the ruling verbatim on the record and move it to whatever the tracker calls 'ready for work'. Do NOT launch the work yourself; the label/comment is the dispatch signal. Report launched:false.
(b) ANSWER IS DEFER (explicit or timer): make NO tracker writes (the record stays parked; a later lap re-asks) — verdict=deferred.
(c) ANSWER DECLINES/KILLS THE QUESTION (won't-fix, moot, superseded): close the record with the ruling cited verbatim in the close reason — verdict=closed.
(d) ANSWER REQUIRES A FRESH RECORD FIRST: file the new record (link it as discovered-from this one), then close THIS record with the ruling cited — verdict=rerouted with new_record_id.
If intake said already_disposed, make no writes and return verdict=deferred with notes citing it. Never invent a decision the owner did not give: the only answer that decides anything is the owner's own release text. Reply with ONLY fenced json {"verdict": "rerouted|closed|deferred", "decision": "<the owner's answer verbatim, or 'defer (timer)'>", "new_record_id": "<id or empty>", "notes": "<one line for the next lap>"}
